notes:
39 stations, lines 5903-5950. The list has no sub-headings, so every row has coast "IRISH COAST" (the section heading).

Format choices:
- Fragments: leading indentation trimmed; everything else, including the spacing inside the line, kept exactly. Where the observers' names wrap, the continuation line ("{   Edward M'Carron.") is its own fragment.
- other: the Sp. and Au. return marks (x / o / --) and the Miles-from-Shore figure are copied exactly, with labels taken from the column headings, e.g. "Sp. x; Au. o; Miles from Shore 8". "_No reply._" and "No schedule sent." are added as printed.
- Keepers: the row-final full stop and joining "and" are removed, e.g. "Hugh J. Dugan and / Edward M'Carron." becomes "Hugh J. Dugan", "Edward M'Carron". Abbreviations like "Wm." and "Robt." are kept.
- The braces "{" only group names that wrap onto a second line. They are not station marks, so marks is null for those rows; the brace stays in the fragments.
- Numbers are given without the printed full stop ("5." becomes "5").

Numbering:
- Two pairs share a number: 5 (Dungarvan) / 5 *Coningbeg Lt.-ship, and 8 (Arklow Sth. Lt.-ship) / 8 *Arklow North Lt.-ship. The asterisk seems to mark an added station using the previous number. Neither row has a footnote, and the abbreviations at the foot don't explain the asterisk.
- Nos. 9, 35 and 36 are missing.

Type and place:
- Only the light-ships have a printed type ("Lt.-ship"). Every other type is null; I did not supply "L.H.".
- "do." (ditto) is kept as the place for Barrels Rock and Tuskar Rock (meaning Wexford) and for Arklow North (meaning Wicklow).
- Tuskar Rock's "do.," sits further right than the place in other rows, but it is the same column.
- "Old Head, Kinsale" is kept as the name, with place "Cork". "Co." appears only for Fastnet ("Co. Cork").

Checks against the abbreviations:
- The counts work out: 27 x in Sp. (7 o), 25 x in Au. (9 o), so 34 sent each season. 39 rows minus the 5 "No schedule sent" also gives 34.
- Lough Swilly is "--" for Sp. but "x" for Au. Oyster Island is "o" for Sp. and "--" for Au. but says "_No reply._".

Possible spellings and cross-references to check (copied as printed):
- "Howth Baily" (usually Baily or Bailey).
- "Innishtrahull" (now Inishtrahull).
- "Arran Island" (Aran).
- "Robert Tyrell".
- "John Pinston".
- "Edward M'Carron" is named at both Mine Head (no. 4) and Tearaght (no. 37). It could be the same keeper moved during the year, or two men.
- "Robt. W. Redmond" (Blacksod Point) and "John Redmond" (Blackrock) share a surname.
